# About Pro

{% hint style="warning" %}
Variational Pro is currently not live.
{% endhint %}

**Variational Pro is designed for advanced and institutional traders of OTC derivatives.**

Pro unlocks the full capabilities of the Variational protocol, allowing traders to access over-the-counter (OTC) liquidity for non-linear derivatives and execute block trades on configurable structures with deep liquidity.

As with traditional finance, a large portion of trading volume in crypto happens via OTC derivatives trading. Crypto (and even certain segments of derivatives trading in traditional finance) still has largely undeveloped infrastructure for booking and settling these OTC trades. Variational Pro addresses this by creating a one-stop-shop for advanced derivatives traders (largely institutions) to automate the execution and settlement of any derivative product they desire.

## Why Variational Pro?

Current institutional crypto derivatives trading (accounting for hundreds of billions or trillions in annual volume) relies heavily on manual OTC processes, often via informal channels like Telegram. While some exchanges like Deribit and tools like Paradigm exist, they lack customization and asset diversity beyond basic options on major cryptocurrencies. This results in high operational overhead for more complex derivatives, with dedicated team members, lawyers, and bank wires required to make any trades.

Most current institutional trading occurs as follows:

1. An institution (Hedge Fund A) decides they want to make a trade on an altcoin option.
2. Knowing that Deribit and others don't support the altcoin they wish to trade, a team at Hedge Fund A uses Telegram to contact a market making desk (Market Maker A).
3. Prior to contacting Market Maker A, Hedge Fund A had to negotiate an ISDA agreement and go through a lengthy KYC process. They were rejected by Market Maker B due to operational constraints, and didn't have time to complete the forms from Market Maker C.
4. Given they only have one desk to choose from, in the Telegram group, Hedge Fund A describes the option structure they're looking to trade with Market Maker A.
5. A team at Market Maker A checks what quote they can offer for the trade Hedge Fund A is looking for, sometimes using manual infrastructure such as spreadsheets.
6. Market Maker A sends the quote and initial terms to Hedge Fund A.
7. Hedge Fund A and Market Maker A debate price/terms and eventually come to agreement.
8. Hedge Fund A and Market Maker A exchange an email trade confirm, which is reviewed by their legal and operations teams.
9. Hedge Fund A's operations team completes a test transaction to the crypto wallet or fiat account of Market Maker A.
10. Hedge Fund A sends funds directly to Market Maker A as collateral, assuming a large amount of counterparty risk if Market Maker A faces financial difficulty.
11. The trade is officially cleared.
12. Every so often, a team at Market Maker A checks up on the trade to ensure margin is topped up and no liquidation is required. Manual margin calls are issued via Telegram and email, though, since they don't have a strong relationship, Market Maker A never posts collateral to Hedge Fund A, even if their trade is winning.

Even with all of this operational lift, institutions still face limited price transparency (i.e. Market Maker A knows that Hedge Fund A has very limited options to book this trade, and can price their quote accordingly), and increased counterparty risk due to infrequent collateral checks and one-way margin requirements. Some risks and inefficiencies of current OTC derivatives trading include:

* **Lack of Market Participants:** Due to the operational overhead required to onboard/KYC, quote, and manage these trades, many smaller market makers and (especially) taker funds limit or outright avoid OTC derivatives trading.
* **Human error:** Since margin checks, collateral movements, and liquidations are manual, firms have limited confidence in trades being managed properly.
* **Counterparty Risk:** Since funds are not automatically moved on-chain with clearly defined rules for real-time pricing and liquidation, institutions are frequently assuming their counterparties will not go bankrupt. [Historically, this is a poor assumption](https://www.reuters.com/business/ftx-start-us-bankruptcy-proceedings-ceo-exit-2022-11-11/) to rely on.

Variational Pro solves these issues by automating the entire trade lifecycle, from booking to on-chain settlement. It offers complete customization for complex derivatives, and allows traders to immediately receive competing quotes from many market makers simultaneously. As opposed to the 12-step, highly manual process above, the process of booking a trade on Variational Pro is the following:

1. An institution (Hedge Fund A) decides they want to make a trade on an altcoin option.
2. Hedge Fund A logs into their Variational Pro account, builds a Request-For-Quote (RFQ) describing the desired trade using the intuitive UI.
3. All market makers on Variational Pro see the RFQ (unless Hedge Fund A has designated specific MMs to request a quote from) and can respond with their best offer, over both the UI and API.
4. Hedge Fund A sees quotes from multiple market makers (Market Maker A, Market Maker B, Market Maker C) and decides which (if any) to accept, considering the counterparty's reputation, the terms of the quote (margin requirements), and more.
5. Once Hedge Fund A chooses to accept a quote (for example, with Market Maker B), Hedge Fund A and Market Maker B are immediately prompted to deposit funds to an on-chain smart contract that functions as their escrow/settlement pool.
6. Once deposits are verified, the trade is automatically marked as cleared. Variational Protocol automatically tracks margin usage, funding payments/settlements (if applicable), and handles liquidations.

Variational Pro takes a process that currently requires Telegram groups, manual transfers/wires and large teams of operations employees and lawyers, and turns it into a safe, on-chain, fully automated flow that can be completed by a single team member or API client.

## How Does Variational Pro Work?

Variational Pro allows for the safe trading of many kinds of bilateral derivatives on any token. Key features include:

* **RFQ-Based:** Users submit a request-for-quote for a specific market/structure they'd like to trade. Liquidity providers respond with quotes and the user may select the best one. Users can also respond to RFQs by providing bids and offers.
* **Bilateral:** All trades are completed peer-to-peer (interchangeably referred to as bilateral or OTC). Trades are booked in settlement pools, which are a ledger of open positions and collateral between two parties. Each unique pair of counterparties will have one (or more) settlement pools. Positions are not fungible between pools, and assets are not commingled between pools, isolating risk.
* **Fully Customizable:** Almost every aspect of the trading, clearing, and settlement process is customizable. Terms are decided before any trade is done and agreed upon by both parties as part of the quote. Market makers compete to offer the best price and terms. Users can decide to only request quotes from a whitelist of counterparties, adjust margin requirements on a per pool basis, or decide to auto liquidate their counterparty when they fall below margin requirements/impose a liquidation penalty.


# Overview

Omni API Documentation. For the OpenAPI specification, see API Specification section.

{% hint style="info" %}
Omni's API is under active development. This means users should expect breaking changes and temporarily low rate limits. Feedback and questions can be shared in the [Variational Discord](https://discord.gg/variational).
{% endhint %}

### Overview

**Omni's API is currently in early access on testnet!** We are releasing an early preview of the API to gather feedback and iterate together with the community. Omni's API is a REST API with intentionally low rate limits to start. Higher limits, additional endpoints, and a websocket API will be released after early access.

### Quickstart

For now, all interactions require an API key to sign requests. You can begin to use the API by creating an API key in the web application, saving the private key to a secure location, and signing requests to the API. The next section, [Usage](https://docs.variational.io/api-documentation/usage), outlines common patterns and includes an overview of endpoints. See [Authentication](https://docs.variational.io/api-documentation/authentication) for how to sign, and [Examples](https://docs.variational.io/api-documentation/examples) for usage examples.

The documentation here is meant to be a non-exhaustive overview of the API and how to use it; including authentication/authorization and usage examples. The authorotative API docs (from our OpenAPI spec) are in the [API Specification](https://docs.variational.io/api-specification/authentication) section.

### Environments

Omni's API will be available in testnet and mainnet, the same as the Omni web application. For now, only testnet is available.

Testnet: `https://api.omni.testnet.variational.io`

Mainnet: coming soon


# Usage

Omni API usage, REST API descriptions, and rate limits/errors.

{% hint style="info" %}
Currently Omni's API is in **early access** and is only available in testnet.
{% endhint %}

### Connecting

```
https://api.omni.testnet.variational.io
```

All endpoints are under `/v1` and need an API key.

### API keys

Create a key from omni in testnet. A key is an Ed25519 key pair:

* The **public key** identifies the key: `0x` followed by 64 hex characters.
* The **private key** signs your requests. Keep it secret.

A key has the `read` scope, and optionally `trade` for placing and cancelling orders. See [Authentication](https://docs.variational.io/api-documentation/authentication) section on how to use the API key to sign requests.

### Reading Market Data

List the instruments you can trade and the rules an order must follow: price precision, size step, minimum notional and margin modes. Tickers give the latest mark and index price for one instrument or all of them.

* `GET /v1/instruments`, `GET /v1/instruments/{symbol}`&#x20;
* `GET /v1/tickers`, `GET /v1/tickers/{symbol}`

### Reading Position & Account Information

Read your account summary (equity, unrealized PnL and margin usage) and your open positions, each with its margin mode, leverage and estimated liquidation price. Values are priced at the time of API call.

* `GET /v1/account`
* `GET /v1/positions`, `GET /v1/positions/{symbol}`

### Placing & Managing Orders

Place market, limit, take-profit and stop-loss orders; a market or limit order can carry its own take-profit and stop-loss. Cancel a single order by its ID or your `client_order_id`, or cancel every pending order at once. Note: these endpoints need a key with the `trade` scope.

* `POST /v1/orders`: place an order. We recommend all interactions include a `client_order_id` to identify the order easily.&#x20;
* `DELETE /v1/orders`: cancel an order
* `DELETE /v1/orders/batch`: cancel every pending order (optionally per-instrument)
* `GET /v1/orders`: list your pending orders (optionally `?symbol=`), or look one up with `?client_order_id=`
* `GET /v1/orders/{order_id}`: read one order by its ID
* `GET /v1/orders/history` to view all orders, newest first (paginated)
* `GET /v1/fills` to view all fills, newest first (paginated)

#### Order format for POST /v1/orders

Orders include a JSON body to specify exactly what order to place. For example, a limit order to buy 1 BTC at 10,000 USDC, with a stop-loss attached at 1,000. Note we always recommend including a `client_order_id` set to a unique string, in the example below this is some bot identifier (`my-bot`) with a unique order number (`0001`).

```json
{
  "type": "limit",
  "symbol": "BTC-PERP",
  "side": "buy",
  "size": "1",
  "price": "10000",
  "trigger_by": "mark",
  "max_slippage": "0.01",
  "client_order_id": "my-bot:0001",
  "stop_loss": {
    "trigger_price": "1000",
    "trigger_by": "mark",
    "max_slippage": null
  }
}
```

The API answers `202` with `{"placed": [...]}`: the order, followed by its stop-loss. A `202` means the order was accepted, not that it filled. Then query `GET /v1/orders/{order_id}`, or `GET /v1/orders?client_order_id=my-bot:0001` to see whether it filled, and `GET /v1/fills` for the fill itself.

| Parameter         | Notes                                                                                                         |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `type`            | `market` · `limit` · `take_profit` · `stop_loss`                                                              |
| `symbol`          | The instrument, e.g. `BTC-PERP`, from `GET /v1/instruments`                                                   |
| `side`            | `buy` or `sell`                                                                                               |
| `size`            | Decimal string in base units, e.g. `"0.5"`. Must be a multiple of the instrument's `size_step`                |
| `price`           | Decimal string in USDC. **`limit` only.** Must satisfy the instrument's `price_precision`                     |
| `trigger_price`   | Decimal string in USDC. **`take_profit` and `stop_loss` only**                                                |
| `trigger_by`      | `mark` or `quote`: the price that triggers the order. Required for every type except `market`                 |
| `max_slippage`    | Fraction of the mark price, e.g. `"0.01"` for 1%. Required; may be `null` for no cap, except on `market`      |
| `reduce_only`     | Optional, default `false`. Not accepted on `take_profit` and `stop_loss`, which are always reduce-only        |
| `client_order_id` | Optional. Your ID: up to 36 letters, digits, `_`, `:` or `-`, **never reused on the account**. Used to cancel |
| `take_profit`     | Optional, `market` and `limit` only. An object of `trigger_price`, `trigger_by` and `max_slippage`            |
| `stop_loss`       | Optional, `market` and `limit` only. Same shape as `take_profit`                                              |

### Rate Limits

Each request contributes some "weight" to a user's usage limit. Currently, every user has 60 weight to spend per minute. The minute is a sliding window: weight you spend comes back 60 seconds after you spent it. Most endpoints cost between 1 and 5 weight.

Every response reports your budget in three headers:

* `X-RateLimit-Limit`: your total weight per window.
* `X-RateLimit-Remaining`: the weight you have left.
* `X-RateLimit-Reset`: when your full budget is back, in Unix seconds.

If you go over the limit, the request is refused with `429` and the error code `rate_limited`. The response's `retry_after_ms` field says how long to wait before retrying.

### Errors

Errors are JSON with a stable `error_code`:

```json
{"error_code": "rate_limited", "error_message": "rate limit exceeded", "retry_after_ms": 1500, "request_id": "..."}
```

When `retry_after_ms` is present, wait that long before retrying. Sign the request again when you retry, so it carries a fresh timestamp.


# Authentication

Omni API authentication/authorization: API keys and signing flow

### Overview

Authentication in Omni's API requires signing your request for certain endpoints (see "signed request" mentioned in the API specification).

### Signing a request

Send three headers with every request:

| Header                    | Value                                           |
| ------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `x-variational-key`       | Your public key.                                |
| `x-request-timestamp-ms`  | The current Unix time in milliseconds.          |
| `x-variational-signature` | `0x` followed by the Ed25519 signature, in hex. |

The signature is over these seven lines, joined by `\n` with no trailing newline:

```
variational-omni-api/v1
testnet
<public key>
<timestamp in ms>
<METHOD>
<path and query, e.g. /v1/tickers/BTC-PERP>
<SHA-256 of the body, in hex>
```

Sign the path and query exactly as you send them. For a request with no body, hash the empty string. The timestamp must be within 5 seconds of the server's clock.

### Example

```python
import hashlib, time, requests
from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.asymmetric.ed25519 import Ed25519PrivateKey

BASE_URL = "https://api.omni.testnet.variational.io"
PUBLIC_KEY = "0x..."
SIGNING_KEY = Ed25519PrivateKey.from_private_bytes(bytes.fromhex("..."))  # 32-byte private key

def call(method, path, body=b""):
    timestamp = str(int(time.time() * 1000))
    canonical = "\n".join([
        "variational-omni-api/v1", "testnet", PUBLIC_KEY, timestamp,
        method, path, hashlib.sha256(body).hexdigest(),
    ])
    headers = {
        "x-variational-key": PUBLIC_KEY,
        "x-request-timestamp-ms": timestamp,
        "x-variational-signature": "0x" + SIGNING_KEY.sign(canonical.encode()).hex(),
    }
    return requests.request(method, BASE_URL + path, headers=headers, data=body)

print(call("GET", "/v1/account").json())
```


# Examples

API examples for signing flow

Every private route of the Variational Trade API takes a request signed with an API key. Each example is one short file that you can copy into your own client.

<table><thead><tr><th width="261">Language</th><th>Needs</th><th data-hidden>File</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>Python</td><td><code>cryptography</code> package</td><td><code>sign.py</code></td></tr><tr><td>TypeScript (Node)</td><td>standard library only</td><td><code>sign.ts</code></td></tr><tr><td>Go</td><td>standard library only</td><td><code>sign.go</code></td></tr><tr><td>Rust</td><td><code>ed25519-dalek</code>, <code>sha2</code> and <code>hex</code> crates</td><td><code>sign.rs</code></td></tr></tbody></table>

## The scheme

An API key is an Ed25519 key pair. You hold the private half as a 32-byte seed, and the server never sees it. The server holds the public half, which is also the key's id: `0x` followed by 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters.

Every signed request carries three headers.

| Header                    | Value                                                                         |
| ------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `x-variational-key`       | The public key, as shown when the key was created.                            |
| `x-request-timestamp-ms`  | The time of the request by your clock: Unix time in milliseconds, an integer. |
| `x-variational-signature` | `0x` and 128 hexadecimal characters: the 64-byte Ed25519 signature.           |

The signature covers one string of seven lines, joined by `\n`, with no newline after the last line.

```
variational-trade-api/v1
<environment>
<public key>
<timestamp in milliseconds>
<METHOD>
<path and query>
<SHA-256 of the body, as 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters>
```

The environment is the name of the deployment you are talking to, for example `prod`. The signature is Ed25519 over the UTF-8 bytes of that string. Ed25519 hashes its input itself, so do not hash the string first.

In Python, the whole of it is this:

```python
canonical = "\n".join([
    "variational-trade-api/v1",
    environment,
    public_key,
    str(timestamp_ms),
    method.upper(),
    path_and_query,
    hashlib.sha256(body).hexdigest(),
])
signature = "0x" + Ed25519PrivateKey.from_private_bytes(seed).sign(canonical.encode()).hex()
```

## A worked example

This is the first case in `vectors.json`. The seed is 32 bytes of `0x33`, a test fixture that controls nothing.

```
request     GET /v1/orders?limit=10&symbol=BTC-PERP on the "test" environment, with no body

canonical   variational-trade-api/v1
            test
            0x17cb79fb2b4120f2b1ec65e4198d6e08b28e813feb01e4a400839b85e18080ce
            1790000000123
            GET
            /v1/orders?limit=10&symbol=BTC-PERP
            e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855

signature   0xda8dd8ca4923a2b75a7852df7dc3bd73bf3e5b079e3a24eef7536a917bb9e9f0c8fe39a3a501311a346df2147f6863420df0437c7a659607bd6e613be6198707
```

## Testing your own signer

Ed25519 signatures are deterministic: the same key and the same message always give the same signature. `vectors.json` therefore lists whole requests together with the exact canonical string and the exact signature each one must produce. The file is the one the server's own tests are held to.

To test a signer in any language:

1. Load `signing_seed` and check that it gives `public_key`.
2. For each case, build the canonical string from `environment`, `public_key`, `timestamp_ms`, `method`, `path_and_query` and the UTF-8 bytes of `body`. Compare it with `canonical`. If they differ, the difference shows which line is wrong.
3. Sign it and compare the result with `signature`.

## Common mistakes

Each of these produces a 401 refusal.

* **Signing different body bytes from the ones sent.** Serialize the JSON once, hash those bytes, and send those same bytes. Serializing a second time can change spacing or key order. A request with no body hashes the empty string.
* **Signing a different path from the one sent.** The path and query are signed exactly as they appear on the request line, including `/v1` and the query string. Do not decode them, do not sort the parameters, and do not leave a trailing `?` on one side only.
* **A clock that is off.** The timestamp must be at most 5,000 ms behind and at most 1,000 ms ahead of the server's clock. A `timestamp_out_of_window` refusal carries `server_time_ms`, which is the server's clock, so a client can correct its offset from that answer.
* **The wrong environment.** A key is registered in one deployment, and the environment's name is part of what is signed. A key from one deployment answers `unknown_key` on another.

## Refusals

A refusal is JSON with `error_code`, `error_message` and `request_id`. The server checks in this order, so the code shows how far the request got.

| Status | `error_code`                 | Meaning                                                           |
| ------ | ---------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 401    | `missing_credentials`        | One of the three headers is absent.                               |
| 401    | `malformed_credentials`      | A header is not in the form above, or was sent twice.             |
| 401    | `timestamp_out_of_window`    | Your clock is off, or the request is stale.                       |
| 401    | `unknown_key`                | No key has this public key in this deployment.                    |
| 401    | `invalid_signature`          | The signature does not verify: the string or the signing differs. |
| 401    | `key_revoked`, `key_expired` | The key is no longer usable.                                      |
| 403    | `insufficient_scope`         | The route needs the `trade` scope and the key grants only `read`. |


# Python

```python
"""Signs a Variational Omni API request. Needs only the `cryptography` package."""
import hashlib

from cryptography.hazmat.primitives import serialization
from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.asymmetric.ed25519 import Ed25519PrivateKey

SCHEME = "variational-omni-api/v1"


def public_key(seed: bytes) -> str:
    """Returns the key's id: `0x` and the 32-byte Ed25519 public key in lowercase hex."""
    raw = Ed25519PrivateKey.from_private_bytes(seed).public_key().public_bytes(
        serialization.Encoding.Raw, serialization.PublicFormat.Raw)
    return "0x" + raw.hex()


def canonical_string(environment: str, key: str, timestamp_ms: int, method: str,
                     path_and_query: str, body: bytes) -> str:
    """Returns the seven lines that are signed, joined by `\\n` with no newline at the end."""
    return "\n".join([
        SCHEME,
        environment,                      # the deployment's name, for example "prod"
        key,                              # exactly as the x-variational-key header spells it
        str(timestamp_ms),
        method.upper(),
        path_and_query,                   # exactly as sent: not decoded, not re-sorted
        hashlib.sha256(body).hexdigest(),  # of the exact body bytes; of b"" when there is none
    ])


def sign_request(seed: bytes, environment: str, method: str, path_and_query: str,
                 body: bytes, timestamp_ms: int) -> dict:
    """Returns the three headers that authenticate one request."""
    key = public_key(seed)
    canonical = canonical_string(environment, key, timestamp_ms, method, path_and_query, body)
    signature = Ed25519PrivateKey.from_private_bytes(seed).sign(canonical.encode())
    return {
        "x-variational-key": key,
        "x-request-timestamp-ms": str(timestamp_ms),
        "x-variational-signature": "0x" + signature.hex(),
    }
```


# Typescript

```typescript
// Signs a Variational Omni API request. Needs only Node's standard library.
import { createHash, createPrivateKey, createPublicKey, sign } from "node:crypto";
import type { KeyObject } from "node:crypto";

const SCHEME = "variational-omni-api/v1";

// The fixed bytes that turn a raw 32-byte Ed25519 seed into the PKCS#8 form Node reads.
const PKCS8_PREFIX = Buffer.from("302e020100300506032b657004220420", "hex");

/** Builds Node's key object from the 32-byte seed. */
function privateKey(seed: Uint8Array): KeyObject {
  return createPrivateKey({
    key: Buffer.concat([PKCS8_PREFIX, seed]),
    format: "der",
    type: "pkcs8",
  });
}

/** Returns the key's id: `0x` and the 32-byte Ed25519 public key in lowercase hex. */
export function publicKey(seed: Uint8Array): string {
  const der = createPublicKey(privateKey(seed)).export({ format: "der", type: "spki" });

  // The raw public key is the last 32 bytes of the encoded form.
  return "0x" + der.subarray(der.length - 32).toString("hex");
}

/** Returns the seven lines that are signed, joined by `\n` with no newline at the end. */
export function canonicalString(
  environment: string,
  key: string,
  timestampMs: number,
  method: string,
  pathAndQuery: string,
  body: Uint8Array,
): string {
  return [
    SCHEME,
    environment, // the deployment's name, for example "prod"
    key, // exactly as the x-variational-key header spells it
    String(timestampMs),
    method.toUpperCase(),
    pathAndQuery, // exactly as sent: not decoded, not re-sorted
    createHash("sha256").update(body).digest("hex"), // of the exact body bytes
  ].join("\n");
}

/** Returns the three headers that authenticate one request. */
export function signRequest(
  seed: Uint8Array,
  environment: string,
  method: string,
  pathAndQuery: string,
  body: Uint8Array,
  timestampMs: number,
): Record<string, string> {
  const key = publicKey(seed);
  const canonical = canonicalString(environment, key, timestampMs, method, pathAndQuery, body);

  // Ed25519 hashes its input itself, so the algorithm argument is null.
  const signature = sign(null, Buffer.from(canonical), privateKey(seed));

  return {
    "x-variational-key": key,
    "x-request-timestamp-ms": String(timestampMs),
    "x-variational-signature": "0x" + signature.toString("hex"),
  };
}
```


# Go

```go
// Package omniapi signs a Variational Omni API request. It needs only the standard library.
package omniapi

import (
	"crypto/ed25519"
	"crypto/sha256"
	"encoding/hex"
	"strconv"
	"strings"
)

const scheme = "variational-omni-api/v1"

// PublicKey returns the key's id: "0x" and the 32-byte Ed25519 public key in lowercase hex.
func PublicKey(seed []byte) string {
	public := ed25519.NewKeyFromSeed(seed).Public().(ed25519.PublicKey)

	return "0x" + hex.EncodeToString(public)
}

// CanonicalString returns the seven lines that are signed, joined by "\n" with no newline at
// the end.
func CanonicalString(environment, key string, timestampMs int64, method, pathAndQuery string, body []byte) string {
	bodyHash := sha256.Sum256(body) // of the exact body bytes; of no bytes when there is no body

	return strings.Join([]string{
		scheme,
		environment, // the deployment's name, for example "prod"
		key,         // exactly as the x-variational-key header spells it
		strconv.FormatInt(timestampMs, 10),
		strings.ToUpper(method),
		pathAndQuery, // exactly as sent: not decoded, not re-sorted
		hex.EncodeToString(bodyHash[:]),
	}, "\n")
}

// SignRequest returns the three headers that authenticate one request.
func SignRequest(seed []byte, environment, method, pathAndQuery string, body []byte, timestampMs int64) map[string]string {
	key := PublicKey(seed)
	canonical := CanonicalString(environment, key, timestampMs, method, pathAndQuery, body)
	signature := ed25519.Sign(ed25519.NewKeyFromSeed(seed), []byte(canonical))

	return map[string]string{
		"x-variational-key":       key,
		"x-request-timestamp-ms":  strconv.FormatInt(timestampMs, 10),
		"x-variational-signature": "0x" + hex.EncodeToString(signature),
	}
}
```


# Rust

```rust
//! Signs a Variational Omni API request.
use ed25519_dalek::{Signer, SigningKey};
use sha2::{Digest, Sha256};

const SCHEME: &str = "variational-omni-api/v1";

/// Holds the three headers that authenticate one request.
pub struct SignedHeaders {
    /// The value of `x-variational-key`.
    pub key: String,
    /// The value of `x-request-timestamp-ms`.
    pub timestamp_ms: String,
    /// The value of `x-variational-signature`.
    pub signature: String,
}

/// Returns the three headers that authenticate one request.
///
/// The `body` argument must hold the exact bytes that are sent, so serialize JSON once and
/// pass the same bytes here and to the HTTP client.
pub fn sign_request(
    seed: &[u8; 32],
    environment: &str,
    method: &str,
    path_and_query: &str,
    body: &[u8],
    timestamp_ms: i64,
) -> SignedHeaders {
    // What is signed.
    let key = public_key(seed);
    let canonical = canonical_string(
        environment,
        &key,
        timestamp_ms,
        method,
        path_and_query,
        body,
    );

    SignedHeaders {
        signature: format!(
            "0x{}",
            hex::encode(
                SigningKey::from_bytes(seed)
                    .sign(canonical.as_bytes())
                    .to_bytes()
            )
        ),
        timestamp_ms: timestamp_ms.to_string(),
        key,
    }
}

/// Returns the key's id: `0x` and the 32-byte Ed25519 public key in lowercase hex.
pub fn public_key(seed: &[u8; 32]) -> String {
    format!(
        "0x{}",
        hex::encode(SigningKey::from_bytes(seed).verifying_key().to_bytes())
    )
}

/// Returns the seven lines that are signed, joined by `\n` with no newline at the end.
pub fn canonical_string(
    environment: &str,
    key: &str,
    timestamp_ms: i64,
    method: &str,
    path_and_query: &str,
    body: &[u8],
) -> String {
    [
        SCHEME,
        // The deployment's name, for example "prod".
        environment,
        // Exactly as the `x-variational-key` header spells it.
        key,
        &timestamp_ms.to_string(),
        &method.to_uppercase(),
        // Exactly as sent: not decoded, not re-sorted.
        path_and_query,
        // The hash of the exact body bytes, or of no bytes when there is no body.
        &hex::encode(Sha256::digest(body)),
    ]
    .join("\n")
}
```


# Authentication

Sign requests with an Ed25519 API key created in Omni, not your wallet key. New keys may take several seconds to become usable. If a newly created key returns `unknown_key`, wait briefly, then retry with a new timestamp and signature.

Include these headers:

* `x-variational-key`: public key (`0x` + 64 hex characters).
* `x-request-timestamp-ms`: Unix timestamp in milliseconds.
* `x-variational-signature`: signature (`0x` + 128 hex characters).

Sign these seven UTF-8 lines with Ed25519, joined by newline characters with no trailing newline. Do not hash the complete string before signing:

```
variational-omni-api/v1
<environment>
<public_key>
<timestamp_ms>
<METHOD>
<path_and_query>
<sha256(body)>
```

Use the environment listed under `servers`, the public key and timestamp exactly as sent in headers, and the uppercase HTTP method. Preserve the path (including `/v1`) and query string exactly. Hash the raw body bytes with SHA-256 and encode the hash as 64 lowercase hex characters; hash the empty string for bodyless requests. Requests with a body require `content-type: application/json`, which is not signed.

The key must grant the endpoint's scope; `trade` includes `read`. The timestamp must be at most 5000 ms behind and at most 1000 ms ahead of the server. On `timestamp_out_of_window`, use `server_time_ms` to correct your clock offset and sign again.

Endpoints requiring `trade` reject reused signatures with `replayed_request`. Read-only endpoints allow repeats. See Errors and retries below.

Offline signing test vector (not a valid API request). The published key controls nothing; `test` is a fixture environment and `/v1/orders` does not accept `limit`.

* Private seed: `0x3333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333333`
* Public key: `0x17cb79fb2b4120f2b1ec65e4198d6e08b28e813feb01e4a400839b85e18080ce`
* Request: `GET /v1/orders?limit=10&symbol=BTC-PERP`, with no body, at timestamp `1790000000123` in the environment `test`

```
variational-omni-api/v1
test
0x17cb79fb2b4120f2b1ec65e4198d6e08b28e813feb01e4a400839b85e18080ce
1790000000123
GET
/v1/orders?limit=10&symbol=BTC-PERP
e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855
```

Expected signature: `0x9f0fd3388c95fcd9ee6e581a03a4757fbd4aeec8cb103731b98e9800e5f9e73ae9c35db7ce6d8df1918a6a3257dd308999f3c695af1670b7d21372b7bf3b600b`.


# Data formats

Decimal values use strings, such as `"0.5"`. Request decimals allow up to 12 decimal places and no scientific notation or JSON numbers. Responses may contain more decimal places; preserve precision when parsing. Units, defaults, and null or omission behavior are documented on individual fields.


# Pagination

Lists return a `results` array. Only `GET /v1/fills` and `GET /v1/orders/history` are paginated, both newest first. Pass a returned `next` or `prev` token as `cursor`, keeping the same filters: `next` reads older results, `prev` newer. Omitted `next` marks the end. An empty page requested with `prev` retains that cursor for polling; an empty page requested with `next` has no cursor. An empty first page has no cursors; repeat the request without `cursor`. Other list endpoints return all results without cursors.


# Errors and retries

Handle `ErrorBody.error_code`, not the changeable `error_message`; use HTTP status for unknown codes. Respect `retry_after_ms` when present. Sign retries with a new timestamp and signature. Unknown routes return `not_found` (404); unsupported methods return `method_not_allowed` (405); `overloaded` (503) includes `retry_after_ms`.

An `outcome_unknown` response means a write may have succeeded. Check `GET /v1/orders/{order_id}` or `GET /v1/orders?client_order_id=YOUR_ID` before retrying; after a batch cancellation, check `GET /v1/orders`. Reuse the original `client_order_id` for placement retries to prevent duplicate orders.


# Compatibility

`/v1` may add endpoints, optional request fields, response fields, and enum values without notice. Ignore unknown response fields and handle unknown enum values. Removals, renames, and semantic changes require a new version path.


# System

API availability and the OpenAPI specification.

> response schemas, authentication requirements, and rate limits.

## Get the API status

> Returns the API's availability: \`ok\`, \`cancel\_only\`, or \`maintenance\`.\
> For individual market status, use \`GET /v1/instruments\`.

```json

# Instruments

Listed instruments and their order requirements.

## List instruments

> Lists all instruments, sorted by symbol. Not paginated.

```json
{"openapi":"3.1.0","info":{"title":"Variational Omni API","version":"1.0.0"},"tags":[{"description":"Listed instruments and their order requirements.","name":"instruments"}],"servers":[{"description":"Production. Sign requests with the environment name `prod`.","url":"https://api.omni.variational.io"},{"description":"Testnet. Sign requests with the environment name `testnet`.","url":"https://api.omni.testnet.variational.io"}],"security":[{"signed_request":["read"]}],"components":{"securitySchemes":{"signed_request":{"description":"Signed requests require an Ed25519 API key. See Authentication in the API overview for signing instructions.","in":"header","name":"x-variational-key","type":"apiKey"}},"parameters":{"XRequestTimestampMs":{"description":"Request time in epoch milliseconds. See Authentication in the API overview for the accepted window.","in":"header","name":"x-request-timestamp-ms","required":true,"schema":{"pattern":"^[0-9]+$","type":"string"}},"XVariationalSignature":{"description":"Ed25519 signature of the request. See Authentication in the API overview for the string to sign.","in":"header","name":"x-variational-signature","required":true,"schema":{"pattern":"^0x[0-9a-fA-F]{128}$","type":"string"}}},"schemas":{"Page_Instrument":{"description":"Results in the endpoint's documented order.","properties":{"next":{"description":"Cursor for the next page. Omitted at the end of the results and for lists that are not paginated.","type":["string","null"]},"prev":{"description":"Cursor for the previous page. Omitted on an empty first page and for unpaginated lists.","type":["string","null"]},"results":{"items":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/Instrument"},"type":"array"}},"required":["results"],"type":"object"},"Instrument":{"description":"A listed market and its order requirements. API sizes already use underlying units;\nnotional is `abs(size) * price`. Do not apply the multiplier again.","format":"int32","type":"integer"},"margin_modes":{"items":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/MarginMode"},"type":"array"},"min_notional":{"description":"Minimum order notional in USDC.","type":"string"},"next_close_at":{"description":"Next closing time in the published trading schedule, in epoch milliseconds.\nFor an open market, this is the end of the current session. For a closed market,\nit is the end of the next session. ## Get an instrument

> Returns the instrument identified by \`symbol\`.

```json

# Ticker

Latest mark and index prices.

## List tickers

> Lists prices for all instruments, sorted by symbol. Not paginated.\
> Prices are null until the first quote is received.

## Get a ticker

> Returns the latest prices for \`symbol\`. Prices are null until the first quote is received.

```json

# Account

Account balances and positions valued at current mark prices.

## Get the account summary

> Returns the caller's equity, unrealized PnL, and margin usage at current mark prices,\
> with separate summaries for cross and isolated margin.

```json

> Lists open positions at current mark prices, sorted by symbol. Not paginated.

## Get the position on one market

> Returns the position for a market. If there is no open position, returns a position with\
> zero size, including the market's margin mode and allocated collateral.

```json

# Orders

Placing, canceling, and reading orders.

## List open orders

> Lists \`queued\`, \`open\`, and \`untriggered\` orders, oldest first. Not paginated.\
> Filter by \`symbol\`, or use \`client\_order\_id\` to retrieve one order in any status.\
> The filters cannot be combined; an unknown client ID returns an empty list.

## Place an order

> Places a market, limit, take-profit, or stop-loss order. Market and limit orders may include\
> attached take-profit and stop-loss orders; all are accepted together or none are created.\
> \
> A 202 response confirms acceptance, not execution. Check the order with\
> \`GET /v1/orders/{order\_id}\` or \`GET /v1/orders?client\_order\_id=YOUR\_ID\`.\
> Later execution failures set \`status\` to \`rejected\` with a \`RejectReason\` in \`reason\`;\
> they do not produce an HTTP error. \`RejectReason\` and HTTP \`error\_code\` are separate\
> enums, even where their names overlap.\
> \
> For safe retries, reuse the same \`client\_order\_id\` with a new timestamp and signature.\
> If the order exists, \`duplicate\_client\_order\_id\` includes it in the response.

```

## Cancel an order

> Cancels the order identified by exactly one of \`order\_id\` or \`client\_order\_id\`.\
> Returns that order; its attached orders are canceled shortly afterward with reason\
> \`parent\_canceled\`.\
> \
> Canceling an already canceled order succeeds. Reuse the order identifier on retries;\
> see Errors and retries in the API overview.

```json
{"openapi":"3.1.0","info":{"title":"Variational Omni API","version":"1.0.0"},"tags":[{"description":"Placing, canceling, and reading orders.","name":"orders"}],"servers":[{"description":"Production. ## Cancel all orders

> Cancels all cancelable orders. Supply exactly one of \`all=true\` or \`symbol\`.\
> \
> Orders already executing are omitted and may still fill. Their attached take-profit and\
> stop-loss orders are canceled, potentially leaving new positions without protection.

## List order history

> Lists orders in all statuses, newest first. See Pagination in the API overview.

```json

## Get an order

> Returns one of the account's orders by its identifier, whatever its status.

```json

beyond one of its risk\n  limits.\n- `price_check_failed`: The quote was too far from the mark price, or was on the wrong side of\n  the order's limit price.\n- `trading_disabled`: Trading was # Fills

The account's confirmed trades.

## List fills

> Lists confirmed trades, newest first, including liquidations and other trades without orders.\
> The \`type\` identifies the trade's origin. See Pagination in the API overview.

# Models

## The Account object

```json
{"openapi":"3.1.0","info":{"title":"Variational Omni API","version":"1.0.0"},"components":{"schemas":{"Account":{"description":"Account balances and margin usage at current mark prices, with separate summaries for\ncross and isolated margin. Amounts are denominated in the settlement asset.","properties":{"cross":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/CrossSummary"},"equity":{"description":"Account equity: collateral plus unrealized PnL at current mark prices.","type":"string"},"initial_margin":{"description":"Total initial margin across all open positions.","type":"string"},"isolated":{"description":"One entry per market with allocated collateral, including markets with no open position.","items":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/IsolatedSummary"},"type":"array"},"maintenance_margin":{"description":"Total maintenance margin required across all open positions.","type":"string"},"unrealized_pnl":{"description":"Unrealized profit or loss across all open positions, in USDC. Positive for profit; negative for loss.","type":"string"}},"required":["equity","unrealized_pnl","initial_margin","maintenance_margin","cross","isolated"],"type":"object"},"CrossSummary":{"description":"Balances and margin usage for collateral not allocated to an isolated market.","properties":{"available":{"description":"Collateral available for new cross-margin exposure: cross balance minus initial margin,\nafter removing any credit from negative isolated collateral allocations. Negative values\nindicate a shortfall. Amounts are in USDC.","type":"string"},"balance":{"description":"Collateral not allocated to isolated markets, plus unrealized PnL on cross-margin\npositions, in USDC. Cross collateral excludes credit from negative\nisolated allocations. This uses cross maintenance margin, unlike `cross.available`,\nwhich uses initial margin. ```

## The AccountLimit object

```json
{"openapi":"3.1.0","info":{"title":"Variational Omni API","version":"1.0.0"},"components":{"schemas":{"AccountLimit":{"description":"One of the account's own limits. Each one caps a notional amount, which is a size multiplied\nby a price, in USDC.\n\n- `gross_notional`: The sum of the absolute notional amounts of the account's positions after\n  the order.\n- `net_notional`: The account's long notional amount minus its short notional amount after the\n  order.\n- `market_notional`: The notional amount of the order itself, compared with the account's\n  limit for the market. It counts the order alone, not the position that the order adds to.\n- `leverage_tier_notional`: The notional amount of the account's position on the market after\n  the order, compared with the maximum of the account's margin tier.","enum":["gross_notional","net_notional","market_notional","leverage_tier_notional"],"type":"string"}}}}

## The CancelReason object

```json
{"openapi":"3.1.0","info":{"title":"Variational Omni API","version":"1.0.0"},"components":{"schemas":{"CancelReason":{"description":"Why an order was canceled.\n\n- `user_canceled`: The account canceled the order.\n- `parent_canceled`: The parent order of this attached take-profit or stop-loss order was canceled.\n- `parent_rejected`: The parent order of this attached take-profit or stop-loss order was rejected.\n- `no_position_to_reduce`: The order was reduce-only, and no position was left to reduce.\n- `reduce_only_wrong_side`: The order was reduce-only, and it was on the side that would have\n  increased the position.\n- `reduce_only_exceeds_position`: The order was reduce-only, and it was larger than the\n  position that was left.\n- `market_delisted`: The order's market was delisted.\n- `system_canceled`: The system canceled the order, for example because the order could no\n  longer be executed.","enum":["user_canceled","parent_canceled","parent_rejected","no_position_to_reduce","reduce_only_wrong_side","reduce_only_exceeds_position","market_delisted","system_canceled"],"type":"string"}}}}

For a closed market,\nit is the end of the next session. An order whose price or trigger price exceeds these\nlimits is refused as `invalid_price_increment`. Round prices to the required precision before\nsubmitting an order.\n\nFor `min_decimal_figures = 2`, `max_decimal_only_figures = 4`, and\n`max_significant_figures = 6`:\n\n| Price | Accepted? | Reason |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| `\"123456.78\"` | Yes | Two decimal places are always allowed for prices of 1 or more. |\n| `\"123.456\"` | Yes | More than two decimal places, but only six significant digits. |\n| `\"123.4567\"` | No | More than two decimal places and more than six significant digits. |\n| `\"0.001234\"` | Yes | Four significant digits; leading zeros do not count. |\n| `\"0.0012345\"` | No | Five significant digits for a price below 1. |\n\nTrailing decimal zeros do not affect validation.","properties":{"max_decimal_only_figures":{"description":"Maximum significant digits for prices below 1. ```

## The IsolatedSummary object

```json
{"openapi":"3.1.0","info":{"title":"Variational Omni API","version":"1.0.0"},"components":{"schemas":{"IsolatedSummary":{"description":"Collateral, balance, and margin usage for one isolated market at current mark prices.","properties":{"allocated":{"description":"Collateral allocated to this isolated market.","type":"string"},"available":{"description":"Collateral available for new exposure in this market, in USDC. Calculated as cross\ncollateral above its maintenance margin plus this market's `balance` minus its\n`initial_margin`, floored at zero. Cross collateral excludes credit from negative\nisolated allocations. This uses cross maintenance margin, unlike `cross.available`,\nwhich uses initial margin. Returns zero if this market's balance is negative.","type":"string"},"balance":{"description":"Allocated collateral plus the position's unrealized PnL.","type":"string"},"initial_margin":{"description":"Initial margin required for these positions, in USDC.","type":"string"},"maintenance_margin":{"description":"Maintenance margin required to keep these positions open, in USDC.","type":"string"},"symbol":{"type":"string"}},"required":["symbol","allocated","balance","initial_margin","maintenance_margin","available"],"type":"object"}}}}
```

## The MarginMode object

```json
{"openapi":"3.1.0","info":{"title":"Variational Omni API","version":"1.0.0"},"components":{"schemas":{"MarginMode":{"description":"Margin mode: `cross` uses shared cross-margin collateral; `isolated` uses collateral\nallocated to the position's market. A position is isolated when its market only trades\nisolated, as a swap does, or when collateral is allocated to the market; cross otherwise.","enum":["cross","isolated"],"type":"string"}}}}
```

## The Order object

```json
{"openapi":"3.1.0","info":{"title":"Variational Omni API","version":"1.0.0"},"components":{"schemas":{"Order":{"description":"Order details, including its type and current status. A field that applies to the\norder's `type` and `status` is always present, and is null when it has no value. A field that\ndoes not apply is omitted.","properties":{"client_order_id":{"description":"Client-supplied order identifier. Present when `status` is `filled`.","type":"string"},"max_slippage":{"description":"How far the fill price may be from the mark price, as a fraction of the mark price. For\nexample, `\"0.01\"` allows a fill up to 1% away. Null when the order sets no limit.","type":["string","null"]},"order_id":{"format":"uuid","type":"string"},"parent_order_id":{"description":"Identifier of the parent order for an attached take-profit or stop-loss order.\nNull for standalone orders.","format":"uuid","type":["string","null"]},"price":{"description":"Limit price, in USDC. Present when `status` is `rejected` or `canceled`.","oneOf":[{"type":"null"},{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/RejectReason"},{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/CancelReason"}]},"reduce_only":{"description":"Whether the order may only reduce an existing position, and never open or increase one.","type":"boolean"},"side":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/Side"},"size":{"description":"Order size, in units of the underlying asset. Null for an order that takes the size of the\nposition when it triggers and has not triggered yet.","type":["string","null"]},"status":{"description":"Current order status and execution or cancellation details.\n\n- `queued`: Execution pending or in progress; cannot be canceled. Market orders enter this state on placement, other orders when execution starts. Remains queued until filled or rejected.\n- `open`: A limit order that is waiting for the price to reach its limit price.\n- `untriggered`: A take-profit, stop-loss, or stop-limit order that is waiting for its trigger.\n- `filled`: The order was filled.\n- `rejected`: The order was rejected while it was being executed.\n- `canceled`: The order was canceled.","enum":["queued","open","untriggered","filled","rejected","canceled"],"type":"string"},"symbol":{"description":"Instrument symbol, retained after delisting. Present when `type` is `take_profit`, `stop_loss`, or `stop_limit`.","type":"string"},"type":{"description":"Order type and associated price parameters.\n\n- `market`: A market order, which is executed as soon as it is placed.\n- `limit`: A limit order, which waits until the price reaches its limit price.\n- `take_profit`: A take-profit order, which waits until the price reaches its trigger price.\n- `stop_loss`: A stop-loss order, which waits until the price reaches its trigger price.\n- `stop_limit`: A stop-limit order. Stop-limit orders can be placed only through the web app, and this API shows them when it lists the account's orders.","enum":["market","limit","take_profit","stop_loss","stop_limit"],"type":"string"}},"required":["order_id","client_order_id","parent_order_id","symbol","side","size","reduce_only","max_slippage","created_at","type","status"],"type":"object"},"RejectDetail":{"description":"The account limit that a rejected order would have exceeded, with the amounts involved.","properties":{"limit":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/AccountLimit"},"max":{"description":"The limit, as a notional amount in USDC.","type":"string"},"value":{"description":"The notional amount, in USDC, that the order would have brought the account to. The\n`limit` field says which notional amount this is.","type":"string"}},"required":["limit","max","value"],"type":"object"},"AccountLimit":{"description":"One of the account's own limits. Each one caps a notional amount, which is a size multiplied\nby a price, in USDC.\n\n- `gross_notional`: The sum of the absolute notional amounts of the account's positions after\n  the order.\n- `net_notional`: The account's long notional amount minus its short notional amount after the\n  order.\n- `market_notional`: The notional amount of the order itself, compared with the account's\n  limit for the market. It counts the order alone, not the position that the order adds to.\n- `leverage_tier_notional`: The notional amount of the account's position on the market after\n  the order, compared with the maximum of the account's margin tier.","enum":["gross_notional","net_notional","market_notional","leverage_tier_notional"],"type":"string"},"RejectReason":{"description":"Why an order was rejected.\n\n- `slippage_exceeded`: The fill price was beyond the order's `max_slippage`.\n- `insufficient_margin`: The account did not have enough margin for the fill.\n- `reduce_only_violated`: The order was reduce-only and would have increased the position.\n- `invalid_order`: The order failed validation while it was being executed.\n- `quote_unavailable`: The liquidity provider declined the order, or its quote expired before\n  the order was filled.\n- `settlement_failed`: The trade could not be settled.\n- `account_limit_exceeded`: The fill would have taken the account beyond its position limits.\n- `leverage_limit_exceeded`: The fill would have taken the account beyond its leverage limit\n  for the market.\n- `market_limit_exceeded`: The fill would have taken the market beyond one of its risk\n  limits.\n- `price_check_failed`: The quote was too far from the mark price, or was on the wrong side of\n  the order's limit price.\n- `trading_disabled`: Trading was disabled.\n- `market_not_trading`: The market closed or was halted before the order was filled.\n- `internal_error`: An error occurred on Variational's side.","enum":["slippage_exceeded","insufficient_margin","reduce_only_violated","invalid_order","quote_unavailable","settlement_failed","account_limit_exceeded","leverage_limit_exceeded","market_limit_exceeded","price_check_failed","trading_disabled","market_not_trading","internal_error"],"type":"string"},"CancelReason":{"description":"Why an order was canceled.\n\n- `user_canceled`: The account canceled the order.\n- `parent_canceled`: The parent order of this attached take-profit or stop-loss order was canceled.\n- `parent_rejected`: The parent order of this attached take-profit or stop-loss order was rejected.\n- `no_position_to_reduce`: The order was reduce-only, and no position was left to reduce.\n- `reduce_only_wrong_side`: The order was reduce-only, and it was on the side that would have\n  increased the position.\n- `reduce_only_exceeds_position`: The order was reduce-only, and it was larger than the\n  position that was left.\n- `market_delisted`: The order's market was delisted.\n- `system_canceled`: The system canceled the order, for example because the order could no\n  longer be executed.","enum":["user_canceled","parent_canceled","parent_rejected","no_position_to_reduce","reduce_only_wrong_side","reduce_only_exceeds_position","market_delisted","system_canceled"],"type":"string"},"Side":{"description":"The side of an order or a trade: `buy` or `sell`.","enum":["buy","sell"],"type":"string"},"TriggerBy":{"description":"Which price decides when a waiting order is executed. The order's limit price or trigger\nprice is compared with this price.\n\n- `mark`: The market's mark price.\n- `quote`: The price at which the order itself would be filled at that moment.","enum":["mark","quote"],"type":"string"}}}}
```

was left.\n- `market_delisted`: The order's market was delisted.\n- `system_canceled`: The system canceled the order, for example because the order could no\n  longer be executed.","enum":["user_canceled","parent_canceled","parent_rejected","no_position_to_reduce","reduce_only_wrong_side","reduce_only_exceeds_position","market_delisted","system_canceled"],"type":"string"},"Side":{"description":"The side of an order or a trade: `buy` or `sell`.","enum":["buy","sell"],"type":"string"},"TriggerBy":{"description":"Which price decides when a waiting order is executed. The order's limit price or trigger\nprice is compared with this price.\n\n- `mark`: The market's mark price.\n- `quote`: The price at which the order itself would be filled at that moment.","enum":["mark","quote"],"type":"string"}}}}
```

Present when `status` is `rejected` or `canceled`.","oneOf":[{"type":"null"},{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/RejectReason"},{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/CancelReason"}]},"reduce_only":{"description":"Whether the order may only reduce an existing position, and never open or increase one.","type":"boolean"},"side":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/Side"},"size":{"description":"Order size, in units of the underlying asset. Remains queued until filled or rejected.\n- `open`: A limit order that is waiting for the price to reach its limit price.\n- `untriggered`: A take-profit, stop-loss, or stop-limit order that is waiting for its trigger.\n- `filled`: The order was filled.\n- `rejected`: The order was rejected while it was being executed.\n- `canceled`: The order was canceled.","enum":["queued","open","untriggered","filled","rejected","canceled"],"type":"string"},"symbol":{"description":"Instrument symbol, retained after delisting. Stop-limit orders can be placed only through the web app, and this API shows them when it lists the account's orders.","enum":["market","limit","take_profit","stop_loss","stop_limit"],"type":"string"}},"required":["order_id","client_order_id","parent_order_id","symbol","side","size","reduce_only","max_slippage","created_at","type","status"],"type":"object"},"RejectDetail":{"description":"The account limit that a rejected order would have exceeded, with the amounts involved.","properties":{"limit":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/AccountLimit"},"max":{"description":"The limit, as a notional amount in USDC.","type":"string"},"value":{"description":"The notional amount, in USDC, that the order would have brought the account to. The\n`limit` field says which notional amount this is.","type":"string"}},"required":["limit","max","value"],"type":"object"},"AccountLimit":{"description":"One of the account's own limits. Each one caps a notional amount, which is a size multiplied\nby a price, in USDC.\n\n- `gross_notional`: The sum of the absolute notional amounts of the account's positions after\n  the order.\n- `net_notional`: The account's long notional amount minus its short notional amount after the\n  order.\n- `market_notional`: The notional amount of the order itself, compared with the account's\n  limit for the market. It counts the order alone, not the position that the order adds to.\n- `leverage_tier_notional`: The notional amount of the account's position on the market after\n  the order, compared with the maximum of the account's margin tier.","enum":["gross_notional","net_notional","market_notional","leverage_tier_notional"],"type":"string"},"RejectReason":{"description":"Why an order was rejected.\n\n- `slippage_exceeded`: The fill price was beyond the order's `max_slippage`.\n- `insufficient_margin`: The account did not have enough margin for the fill.\n- `reduce_only_violated`: The order was reduce-only and would have increased the position.\n- `invalid_order`: The order failed validation while it was being executed.\n- `quote_unavailable`: The liquidity provider declined the order, or its quote expired before\n  the order was filled.\n- `settlement_failed`: The trade could not be settled.\n- `account_limit_exceeded`: The fill would have taken the account beyond its disabled.\n- `market_not_trading`: The market closed or was halted before the order was filled.\n- `internal_error`: An error occurred on Variational's side.","enum":["slippage_exceeded","insufficient_margin","reduce_only_violated","invalid_order","quote_unavailable","settlement_failed","account_limit_exceeded","leverage_limit_exceeded","market_limit_exceeded","price_check_failed","trading_disabled","market_not_trading","internal_error"],"type":"string"},"CancelReason":{"description":"Why an order was canceled.\n\n- `user_canceled`: The account canceled the order.\n- `parent_canceled`: The parent order of this attached take-profit or stop-loss order was canceled.\n- `parent_rejected`: The parent order of this attached take-profit or stop-loss order was rejected.\n- `no_position_to_reduce`: The order was reduce-only, and no position was left to reduce.\n- `reduce_only_wrong_side`: The order was reduce-only, and it was on the side that would have\n  increased the position.\n- `reduce_only_exceeds_position`: The order was reduce-only, and it was larger than the\n  position that was left.\n- `market_delisted`: The order's market was delisted.\n- `system_canceled`: The system canceled the order, for example because the order could no\n  longer be executed.","enum":["user_canceled","parent_canceled","parent_rejected","no_position_to_reduce","reduce_only_wrong_side","reduce_only_exceeds_position","market_delisted","system_canceled"],"type":"string"},"Side":{"description":"The The order's limit price or trigger\nprice is compared with this price.\n\n- `mark`: The market's mark price.\n- `quote`: The price at which the order itself would be filled at that moment.","enum":["mark","quote"],"type":"string"}}}}
```

# Legacy API

{% hint style="info" %}
The public read API will soon be deprecated in favor of using the read functionality built into the trading API. We encourage builders to begin using the trading API for reads in preparation for this migration.
{% endhint %}

## Read-Only API

Public REST API providing market statistics for Variational Omni.

### Base URL

<https://omni-client-api.prod.ap-northeast-1.variational.io>

### Endpoint

`GET /metadata/v2/stats`

Returns platform-wide and per-listing market statistics for all perpetual and swap markets.

{% hint style="warning" %}
The legacy v1 endpoint, `GET /metadata/stats`, is still available for existing integrations but is not recommended, as it may have incomplete or stale information. For example, its tickers do not say whether a market is a perpetual or a swap, and it reports a placeholder funding rate of `0` for swaps. New integrations should use `/metadata/v2/stats`, and existing ones should [migrate](#migrating-from-v1).
{% endhint %}

### Rate Limits

* Per IP: 10 requests per 10 seconds.
* Global: 1000 requests per minute.

The limits are shared with the legacy v1 endpoint. Requests over the limit receive HTTP `429` with a JSON body whose `retry_after_seconds` field says when to retry.

### Response Fields

#### General Metrics

| Field                      | Type    | Description                                                                                          |
| -------------------------- | ------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `total_volume_24h`         | string  | 24-hour trading volume across all markets (USDC)                                                     |
| `cumulative_volume`        | string  | Lifetime cumulative trading volume (USDC)                                                            |
| `tvl`                      | string  | Total value locked in settlement pools and the OLP vault (USDC)                                      |
| `open_interest`            | string  | Total open interest across all markets (USDC), double-sided: includes both trader and OLP positions  |
| `num_markets`              | integer | Number of listed markets, perpetuals and swaps alike. May exceed the number of entries in `listings` |
| `loss_refund.pool_size`    | string  | Deprecated. Always `0`, as loss refunds have been discontinued                                       |
| `loss_refund.refunded_24h` | string  | Deprecated. Always `0`, as loss refunds have been discontinued                                       |
| `listings`                 | array   | Per-listing statistics                                                                               |

#### Per-Listing Fields

| Field                               | Type           | Description                                                                                                                                                                               |
| ----------------------------------- | -------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ticker`                            | string         | Market ticker, suffixed with the contract type (e.g., `BTC-PERP`, `XAU-SWAP`)                                                                                                             |
| `contract_type`                     | string         | `perpetual` or `swap`. Determines the shape of `funding`                                                                                                                                  |
| `name`                              | string         | Asset name (e.g., `Bitcoin`)                                                                                                                                                              |
| `mark_price`                        | string         | Current mark price                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `volume_24h`                        | string         | 24h trading volume (USDC)                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `open_interest.long_open_interest`  | string         | Long open interest (USDC), single-sided: trader positions only                                                                                                                            |
| `open_interest.short_open_interest` | string         | Short open interest (USDC), single-sided: trader positions only                                                                                                                           |
| `funding`                           | object or null | Current funding terms. See [Perpetual Funding Fields](#perpetual-funding-fields) and [Swap Funding Fields](#swap-funding-fields). `null` when no funding data is available for the market |
| `base_spread_bps`                   | string         | Bid/ask spread of the smallest quote (`quotes.base`, or `quotes.size_1k` if unavailable), in basis points of the mark price                                                               |
| `quotes`                            | quotes object  | Indicative quotes at several sizes                                                                                                                                                        |

#### Perpetual Funding Fields

Shape of `funding` when `contract_type` is `perpetual`. See [Funding Rates](https://docs.variational.io/omni/trading/funding-rates) for how perpetual funding works.

| Field              | Type                          | Description                                                                |
| ------------------ | ----------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `last`             | perpetual rate object         | Current funding rate                                                       |
| `next`             | perpetual rate object or null | Predicted funding rate for the next interval. Currently the same as `last` |
| `interval_seconds` | integer                       | Funding interval in seconds                                                |
| `next_timestamp`   | integer                       | Time of the next funding payment (Unix seconds)                            |

Each perpetual rate object contains the same rate in two units. A positive rate means longs pay shorts; a negative rate means shorts pay longs.

| Field             | Type   | Description                           |
| ----------------- | ------ | ------------------------------------- |
| `annualized_rate` | string | Annualized funding rate               |
| `interval_rate`   | string | Funding rate for one funding interval |

#### Swap Funding Fields

Shape of `funding` when `contract_type` is `swap`. Swap funding is paid once per trading day, with separate rates for longs and shorts. See [Swaps Funding](https://docs.variational.io/omni/trading/swaps#swaps-funding) for how it works.

| Field              | Type                     | Description                                                                                                    |
| ------------------ | ------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `last`             | swap rate object or null | Rates of the most recently applied funding payment. `null` if the market has not paid funding in the past week |
| `next`             | swap rate object or null | Rates of the upcoming funding payment. `null` between a payment and the publication of the next one's rates    |
| `interval_seconds` | integer                  | Always `86400` (one payment per trading day)                                                                   |
| `next_timestamp`   | integer or null          | Time the `next` payment applies (Unix seconds). `null` when `next` is `null`                                   |

At least one of `last` and `next` is present; a swap market with neither reports `funding` as `null`.

Each swap rate object contains:

| Field                   | Type   | Description                                                                   |
| ----------------------- | ------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `annualized_long_rate`  | string | Annualized rate for long positions. Positive means longs pay                  |
| `annualized_short_rate` | string | Annualized rate for short positions. Positive means shorts receive            |
| `interval_long_rate`    | string | Rate for long positions for one payment (the annualized rate divided by 360)  |
| `interval_short_rate`   | string | Rate for short positions for one payment (the annualized rate divided by 360) |

Payments that cover weekends or market holidays include the closed days, so their rates read about 3× those of a regular day.

#### Quotes Fields

| Field        | Type         | Description                                                       |
| ------------ | ------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `updated_at` | string       | Time the quotes were fetched (ISO 8601)                           |
| `base`       | quote object | Quote at the market's minimum order size                          |
| `size_1k`    | quote object | Quote at $1,000 notional                                          |
| `size_100k`  | quote object | Quote at $100,000 notional                                        |
| `size_1m`    | quote object | Quote at $1,000,000 notional (major and high-volume markets only) |

#### Quote Fields

| Field | Type   | Description |
| ----- | ------ | ----------- |
| `bid` | string | Bid price   |
| `ask` | string | Ask price   |

### Example

#### Python

```python
# /// script
# requires-python = ">=3.9"
# dependencies = ["requests"]
# ///

import requests

BASE_URL = "https://omni-client-api.prod.ap-northeast-1.variational.io"

def fetch_stats():
    resp = requests.get(f"{BASE_URL}/metadata/v2/stats")
    resp.raise_for_status()
    return resp.json()

def describe_funding(listing):
    funding = listing["funding"]
    if funding is None:
        return "no funding data"
    if listing["contract_type"] == "perpetual":
        rate = float(funding["last"]["annualized_rate"])
        return f"{rate:.2%} annualized"
    # Swaps: prefer the upcoming payment once its rates are published
    rates = funding["next"] or funding["last"]
    long_rate = float(rates["annualized_long_rate"])
    short_rate = float(rates["annualized_short_rate"])
    return f"long {long_rate:.2%} / short {short_rate:.2%} annualized"

stats = fetch_stats()

# Platform metrics
print(f"24h Volume: ${float(stats['total_volume_24h']):,.2f}")
print(f"TVL: ${float(stats['tvl']):,.2f}")
print(f"Open Interest: ${float(stats['open_interest']):,.2f}")
print(f"Markets: {stats['num_markets']}")

# List all markets
print("\nListings:")
for listing in stats["listings"]:
    print(f"  {listing['ticker']}: ${listing['mark_price']}, funding {describe_funding(listing)}")
```

You may save the script as `omni_stats.py` and run it directly with [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/):

```bash
uv run omni_stats.py
```

### Migrating from v1

`/metadata/v2/stats` reports the same platform-wide metrics as `/metadata/stats`. Only the per-listing fields differ:

* `ticker` is suffixed with the contract type, e.g., `BTC` becomes `BTC-PERP`. Swaps are listed under their displayed symbol, e.g., `XAUS` becomes `XAU-SWAP`.
* `contract_type` is new.
* `funding` replaces `funding_rate` and `funding_interval_s`. For perpetuals, v1's `funding_rate` corresponds to `funding.last.annualized_rate`, and `funding_interval_s` to `funding.interval_seconds`. Swaps, which v1 reports with a placeholder rate of `0`, now report their actual long and short rates.
* A market without funding data reports `funding` as `null` rather than a funding rate of `0`.

### Notes

* All numeric values are returned as strings to preserve decimal precision.
* The bid/ask price may be cached for up to 600 seconds, all quotes contain an `updated_at` field.
* Prices and volumes are denominated in USDC.
* Funding rates are decimals (multiply by 100 for percentage).
* `quotes.updated_at` is an ISO 8601 string, while funding timestamps are Unix seconds.
* `name`, `base_spread_bps`, `quotes`, and the individual quote sizes are omitted when unavailable, e.g., while a swap market is closed. `funding` is always present, and is `null` when unavailable.

For questions, [contact support through one of our official channels](https://docs.variational.io/more/getting-help-support).

# Trade and Transfer History

CSV downloads are available by clicking the download icon on each page in one's portfolio. Users can download CSVs of their historical trades, funding, realized PnL, and transfers from Omni (up to a 365-day window).

{% hint style="info" %}
Pending items are not included in CSV exports, and only up to 10,000 rows will be exported at once.
{% endhint %}

### Trades

The following data is included in each row of the trades CSV:

| Column                      | Type      | Description                                                                                   |
| --------------------------- | --------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| id                          | string    | Unique identifier for each trade.                                                             |
| created\_at                 | timestamp | Timestamp of trade creation.                                                                  |
| side                        | string    | Always one of: {"buy", "sell"}                                                                |
| instrument\_type            | string    | Always "perpetual\_future"                                                                    |
| underlying                  | string    | Ticker of underlying (e.g. “BTC”).                                                            |
| price                       | decimal   | Execution price of the trade                                                                  |
| qty                         | decimal   | Trade quantity                                                                                |
| trade\_type                 | string    | Always one of: {"trade", "liquidation", "settlement\_market\_delisted"}                       |
| status                      | string    | Always one of: {“confirmed”, “failed”}                                                        |
| liquidation\_trigger\_price | decimal   | If trade\_type is "liquidation," this displays the mark price that triggered the liquidation. |

### Funding, Realized PnL, and Transfers

The following data is included in each row of the transfers CSV:

| Column           | Type      | Description                                                                 |
| ---------------- | --------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| id               | string    | Unique identifier for each transfer.                                        |
| created\_at      | timestamp | Timestamp of transfer creation.                                             |
| qty              | decimal   | Transfer quantity                                                           |
| asset            | string    | Settlement asset for the transfer (e.g. "USDC")                             |
| transfer\_type   | string    | Always one of: {"deposit", "withdrawal", "realized\_pnl", "funding", "fee"} |
| status           | string    | Always "confirmed"                                                          |
| underlying       | string    | Ticker of underlying (e.g. “BTC”).                                          |
| instrument\_type | string    | Always "perpetual\_future"                                                  |
| fee\_type        | string    | Always one of {"trade", "deposit", "withdrawal"}                            |
| funding\_rate    | decimal   | Funding rate at given timestamp                                             |
